at-0001.title: Use BillingError with snake_case codes
at-0001.content: Raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a snake_case code string for domain validation failures, e.g. "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount"; include a short detail string as the second argument.

last_failure.review_comment: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0002.content: When validating integer inputs, explicitly reject bool via isinstance(x, bool) before the int check, since True/False pass isinstance(x, int).

at-0003.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
at-0003.content: In ledgerly, normalize any incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).

at-0004.title: Money operations accept idempotency_key first
at-0004.content: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it first, before any state validation: scan `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an entry with the same key and return the original record without reapplying. Pass `idempotency_key` into the `audit.record(...)` call.

at-0007.title: Record state transitions via audit.record
at-0007.content: Every payment/invoice state transition must emit an `audit.record` event named `<entity>_<action>` (e.g. `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`) carrying the entity id and amount.
